title: Balancer migration prep checkin — weekly journal
content:
Purpose:
Weekly checkpoint for the balancer migration prep workstream — tracking readiness signals across regions, experiments for pre-warm / priority lanes, and handoffs for the cutover sprint. Informal notes, decisions, and owners below.

Attendees (async + live): Maya, Diego, Ravi, Hannah, Liam, oncall-ops (watching), SRE rota: week B.

Quick status TL;DR:
- Migration readiness: 72% across global fleet (per readiness checklist). Remaining blockers concentrated in APAC-east (three edge clusters).
- Canary plan: carved out 10% of traffic to test new balancer in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 next Wed. Need final signoff from SRE lead by EOD Tue.
- Pre-warm experiment: run #4 (time-shifted pre-warm) reduced cold-start tail by ~38ms p95 but increased steady-state token cost by 0.6% in our sample window.
- Priority lanes: prototype working; needs throttling policy and billing alignment.

Metrics snapshot (sampling window: last 72h):
- Global GPU pool utilization: 64% avg, peak 91% (us-east-1 peak surge 04/09 13:20 UTC)
- Cold start events (>200ms extra latency): 92 events total, 57 in APAC-east clusters
- Avg inference latency (p50/p95): 42ms / 118ms; balancing change target: p95 <= 100ms post-migration
- Spare capacity (opportunistic pool): 3.8% global; target >= 5% for canary window

Week accomplishments:
- Diego: completed config conversion for new balancer (ACLs + route-maps) and pushed to staging. Found unexpected env var mismatch for preemption policy; patch PR opened.
- Hannah: ran pre-warm experiment #4 (time-shifted), collected traces, started cost vs latency delta analysis.
- Ravi: validated region failover scripts; found a race in drain logic when scaling down subpools — added guard and unit tests.
- Liam: updated the runbook draft to include priority-lane billing stub and rollback checklist.

Open/blockers (priority order):
1) APAC-east edge clusters: node image mismatch on gpu-drivers (old 550 vs 560 expected) — blocks canary there. Action: Diego to coordinate with infra-image team for fastpatch; target 2028-04-13 23:59 UTC.
2) Spare capacity <5% in us-west-2 during business hours — need temporary pledge of reserved capacity or shift lower-priority workloads. Action: Ops to reserve 16 gpus from Dedicated pool for Wed canary (Ravi owner).
3) Billing alignment for priority lanes unclear — product needs to sign off on how to attribute burst vs standard traffic. Action: Maya to sync with Product Billing (pinged billing@redwood, meeting 2028-04-12).

Decisions made this week:
- Canary percentage set to 10% traffic split; fallback threshold p95 latency + error delta = 15% relative increase triggers automated rollback.
- Pre-warm policy will be opt-in per model route for the canary. If cost delta > 1.2% for any route, pre-warm disabled for that route in canary.
- Priority lanes will use token-based throttles with a separate capacity band (soft reservation). Billing will be tracked via a new usage tag (priority_lane=true).

Runbook / Playbook notes (current draft pointers):
- preflight checklist: node image versions, driver kernel ABI, NTP drift <500ms, kv-cache compatibility check, model-quantization-compat matrix validated.
- cutover window: Wed 02:00–04:00 UTC (low traffic); warm-up job kicks at 01:30 UTC.
- rollback steps: disable balancer config, shift 100% back to legacy lb, scale up legacy pool +2x for 5m, open investigation ticket.

Experiment notes (detail):
- Pre-warm #4 (time-shifted): spawn light-weight warmers 10m before expected peak per region. Pros: reduced tail latency for models with short prefix reuse. Cons: slightly higher token spend due to warmers left active longer during mispredicted peaks.
- Alternative (trace-driven pre-warm): use per-route trace classifier to predict 30s bursts — more complex but lower steady cost. Prototype backlog item CAP-881.

Risk matrix (top 5):
- Driver mismatch in APAC-east -> medium-high -> mitigation: hold cluster from canary until patched + manual capacity reroute.
- Unexpected p95 regressions due to route-map misclassification -> medium -> mitigation: smaller canary, increased observability on route decisions.
- Billing disputes on priority lanes -> medium -> mitigation: capture detailed logs and stub billing reports pre-cutover.
- Overcommit on spare pool from other teams -> low-medium -> mitigation: short-term Dedicated pledge + quota lock.
- Rollback automation bugs -> low -> mitigation: manual rollback rehearsals scheduled Tue.

Action items (owner / due / status):
- Diego: patch node image for APAC-east + coordinate fastpatch (due 2028-04-13) / in_progress
- Ravi: reserve 16 Dedicated GPUs in us-west-2 for Wed canary (due 2028-04-12) / todo
- Maya: sync with Product Billing and confirm priority_lane tagging and cost attribution (due 2028-04-12) / todo
- Hannah: finalize pre-warm cost analysis and produce route-level report (due 2028-04-12) / in_progress
- Liam: add rollback rehearsal checklist to runbook and schedule rehearsal (due 2028-04-12) / todo

Notes to self / scratchpad (raw):
- If APAC-east patch slips, consider moving APAC canary to APAC-southeast and adjust latency guardrails; check downstream customers in that region (top 10 by usage).
- Check whether short-lived warmers can be run as spot jobs on Dedicated pools to reduce billed tokens.
- Slack threads: #infra-balancer (pin: canary-traffic-graph), #oncall-runbook (link to rehearsal schedule).

Postmortem anchors (for after canary if needed):
- capture: full trace sample 30m pre and 60m post cutover, cpu/gpu metrics, queue depth histograms, route-decision logs, billing diff report.
- timeline: use event-sourced timeline (kibana trace ids) + manual notes from runbook lead.

Next sync / cadence:
- Daily async updates on the doc + 30m live huddle Tue 10:00 UTC for final signoff.

Appendix (useful links):
- Prior design notes: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/BALANCER-DESIGN-2
- Canary dashboard (staging): grafana.redwood.ai/d/balancer-canary
- Related Jira: INF-4721 (balancer config convert), CAP-881 (pre-warm prototype)

End of note.

-- maya
